# *Preface.*

## Courteous Reader!

The majority of scholars and those experienced and well-versed in the <term>Hermetic science<note>The tradition of alchemy and natural philosophy named after the legendary figure Hermes Trismegistus.</note></term> will acknowledge me for this concise yet substantial little treatise. Even though it consists of only a few <term>printer's sheets<note>original: "Alphabeten"; a term referring to the sets of signatures (A-Z) used to measure the length of a printed book.</note></term>, it contains more regarding the chemical-philosophical science than an entire large volume filled with shells without kernels. Within these pages—provided they are read through—is revealed, out of Christian love for one’s neighbor, the entire <term>Theophrastic-medical secret<note>Refers to the medical and alchemical teachings of Paracelsus (Theophrastus von Hohenheim).</note></term>. This includes the true and naturally fundamental dissolution of gold—achieved <term>without corrosiveness<note>original: "absque Corrosivitate".</note></term> and remaining irreducible—as a uniform <term>drinkable gold<note>original: "Aurum potabile"; a legendary alchemical remedy believed to be a universal medicine.</note></term>, suitable for all illnesses, even the most desperate and dangerous. Furthermore, it reveals the reduction of <term>common mercury<note>original: "Mercurii communis"; ordinary quicksilver.</note></term> back into its first essence as a crystal-clear water, without which nothing fruitful can be accomplished in true chemistry. This knowledge is shared to bring greater honor and fame to all <term>physicians<note>original: "Medicis".</note></term>, better security to all <term>chemists<note>original: "Chymicis".</note></term> so they do not labor in vain, great benefit to jewelers and goldsmiths, and a more successful <term>cure<note>original: "Cur".</note></term> for the patients of <term>surgeons<note>original: "Chirurgis".</note></term>.

...will give their approval that it may be learned. For through such a small work of love—acting as a **Master Key**—all of **Theophrastus Paracelsus’** <term>hieroglyphic-medical<note>Refers to a system where medical substances and processes are encoded in symbols or "hieroglyphs" to keep them secret from the uninitiated.</note></term> and enigmatic-philosophical locks, or his obscure and secret ways of speaking, are opened, explained, and unlocked. Therefore, to help the seeker reach this great secret, this highly polished **Theophrastian** Master Key to the <term>Hermetic-philosophical<note>The "Hermetic" tradition refers to alchemy and the hidden laws of nature, named after the legendary sage Hermes Trismegistus.</note></term> door is herewith handed over and shared in **God’s** name, to His highest praise and honor. 

By this key, one may enter the everlasting garden of the **Hesperides** <note>In Greek mythology, a garden producing golden apples; here, an alchemical metaphor for the place where the "Great Work" is perfected.</note> to pluck the golden and silver apples from the trees standing there in full bloom. One may also enter to heal **Jason’s** old father <note>The text likely refers to Aeson, Jason's father, whom the sorceress Medea restored to youth using a potion of herbs. Alchemists used this myth as a metaphor for the rejuvenating power of the Philosopher’s Stone.</note> with the potion that **Medea** gathered and prepared from all sorts of herbs in this garden under the full moon, thereby curing all infirmities of the body. 

In this garden, the seeker will further behold: 
1. The gathered blood of **Pyramus** and **Thisbe**, with which white mulberries are stained red; 
2. The blood of **Ajax**, from which the everlasting **Hyacinth** flower grows, and the blood of the giants caused by the thunderbolts of the god **Jove**; 
3. And the blood of **Adonis**, which is transformed into the **Anemone** rose by the goddess **Venus** who descended there. 

Furthermore, the seeker will be greatly amazed and delighted by: 
4. The wondrous bath of the naked goddess **Diana** found in this oft-mentioned philosophical garden, and the **doves** hovering above it; 
5. The fountain of **Narcissus**; 
6. **Scylla**, who walks without clothes in this **Sea of Wisdom** because of the excessive heat of the sun; 
7. The **Lydian** river **Pactolus**, which turned into pure gold after **Midas Mygdonius** washed himself in it; 
8. And the river **Numicius**, in which **Aeneas**—by command of the goddess **Venus**—was washed of his mortality and translated into immortality. 

Finally, one will marvel at the many tears of **Althaea** after she took off her golden garments and laid them aside in this divine bath of the Sages. Now, when a **Physician** <note>original: "Medicus"</note> desires to earn honor and serve both **God** and his suffering neighbor...

# Preface.

...of the patient or is eager to observe the love of one’s neighbor, then through this quite compendious opening, a bright-shining light will be lit for him. By this light, such a person will be able to look into the most dangerous cases of illness and not only cure them fundamentally <note>original: *radicitus*; meaning to pull the disease out by its roots</note>, but also be able to transform the imperfect metals into the most perfect state. 

To those chemists <note>original: *Chymicis*</note>, however, who are partly infected by sophistry <note>In this context, "sophistry" refers to false alchemical practices—those who use trickery or focus only on material recipes without understanding the deeper natural laws.</note>, or even entirely drowned in it, and who wish to transmute body through body, I say as a point of note <note>original: *pro notamine*</note> from a free and faithful heart—and indeed, as **Theophrastus Paracelsus** speaks in the *Seventh Book of the Transmutation of Natural Things* <note>original: *Libro septimo de Transmutatione Rerum naturalium*</note>, for the better certainty of their faith—that transformation is a great natural mystery of a metallic nature, and not against the course of nature or **God’s** order, as many people falsely believe. For imperfect metals can be transformed into neither gold nor silver without the science and knowledge of the **Philosopher’s Stone**; thus far **Theophrastus**. 

Likewise: In the *Manual* <note>Refers to Paracelsus’s *Manual on the Philosophical Stone*.</note> he says concerning the medicinal **Philosopher’s Stone**: "Our Stone is a heavenly medicine and more than perfect, because it washes away the filth of all metals," etc. Whereby it is also chiefly to be noted that a lover devoted to <term>Hermetic philosophy<note>The study of the hidden laws of nature and alchemy, named after the legendary figure Hermes Trismegistus.</note></term> can attain a perfect knowledge from the published writings of **Theophrastus Paracelsus** as well as from other <term>Adepts<note>original: *Adeptorum*; those who have mastered the "Great Work" of alchemy.</note></term> and true owners of this divine science <note>original: *Scienz*</note>. 

Therefore, I hope that a Hermetic-philosophical world will not look upon this disclosure—made by me in good heart (though many will take offense at me for it)—with unfavorable eyes, but rather consider it quite favorably, seeing that this has happened from no other purpose than pure love of neighbor. I wish that no useless costs be spent, and that one may work according to the intention and teaching of **Theophrastus**, serving both oneself and one's fellow man. To those esteemed worthy of this by **God** and engaged in this science, I wish a happy success <note>original: *Success*</note>, and then also a joyfully blessed outcome and end.

### First Paragraph.
### Concerning the Separation of the Elements.

*In all things of Nature, four elements lie hidden.* <note>original: *In omnibus Naturae Rebus quatuor latent Elementa.*</note> **That is:** In all tangible matter, in the macrocosm <note>the "great world" or the universe at large</note> as well as the microcosm <note>the "little world," usually referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe</note>, four elements are mixed together. In every single thing, however, only one among the four is fixed and perfect; this is then the predestined element, in which the <term>quintessence</term> <note>original: *quinta Essentia*; the purest and most concentrated essence of a substance, believed to be its medicinal or spiritual core</note>, power, and quality reside. The remaining three elements are simple, base, and imperfect, and possess no other virtue than that of any other mere element, for they are only the dwelling place of the true, fixed, and perfect element. Because of this, they are called only <term>qualified things</term> <note>original: *Res qualificatae*; substances that possess certain characteristics but lack the primary "fixed" power of the quintessence</note>.

But the reason one might think the <term>body</term> <note>original: *Corpus*; the physical, tangible substance of a thing</note> itself is the true element, or the quality itself, and that the virtue of the true element shows itself to some extent, is because the bo-

<summary>This page introduces the foundational concept of Paracelsian alchemy: that all matter contains four elements, but only one "predestined element" holds the concentrated quintessence or power. The other three elements serve merely as a physical housing or "body" for this central virtue.</summary>
<keywords>separation of elements, quintessence, macrocosm, microcosm, Paracelsus, predestined element, four elements, alchemy</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the separation of elements. The first word, "body" (completing "Corpus" from the previous page), refers to the physical substance being treated. The text moves from theoretical element theory to the practical necessity of destroying the physical "house" of a substance to release its inner "inhabitant" or essence.</meta>

body, as the three imperfect *elements* are tinctured <note>original: *tingirt*; to be imbued with a quality or color, a fundamental alchemical concept of transformation</note> and characterized by the fixed and perfect, as well as the *predestined* element, or *quintessence*, as its inhabitants. This occurs each according to its own kind: in some, the *element of water* predominates and rules; in some bodies, however, the element of fire is most prominent; in some, the element of earth; and in some, the element of air.

When the fixed-*predestined* element is to be separated from its dwelling, the "house" must necessarily be destroyed and broken apart. This happens in various ways, as is clearly stated in *The Metamorphosis concerning the Death of Things* <note>original: *Metamorphosi de morte rerum*; a work attributed to Paracelsus describing how substances change form or "die" to be reborn in a purer state</note>. It explains that once the house is destroyed and broken through *solutions* <note>dissolving a solid into a liquid</note>, *calcinations* <note>reducing a substance to powder or ash through heat</note>, and the like, it is vital to *observe* that the destroyed matter must then be separated from the fixed part through common *distillations*. This is done so that the *body* is led over the <term>helm</term> <note>original: *Helm*; the top part of a still or alembic where vapors collect</note> in the manner of <term>phlegm</term> <note>original: *Phlegma*; in alchemy, the watery, tasteless distillate that lacks the "spirit" of the substance</note> away from the *quintessence*, leaving the "fifth essence" or fixed element behind at the bottom of the vessel. And since we do not value or desire the "house," but seek only its inhabitant, that inhabitant must be found in the fixed-predestined element. It must be drawn out in the manner of a *quintessence*, using sharper manual operations (beyond mere *calcinations* and *sublimations* <note>heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again to purify it</note>) to destroy the fixed element and separate the pure part from the impure.

The pure part then is the true *quintessence*; the impure, however, is the surplus, or the <term>tartaric essence</term> <note>original: *tartarisches Wesen*; Paracelsus used "tartar" to describe the waste products or impurities that cause blockages and disease, comparing them to the hard deposits left by wine in a barrel</note>, which clings to every birth and is mixed with it. Concerning this, one should consult the book *On Tartaric Diseases* <note>original: *de Morbis tartareis*</note>.

And because this theory is also extensively set out in the remaining books of *Theophrastus Paracelsus* <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), the famous Swiss physician and alchemist</note>, such as: *The Archidoxis* <note>original: *Archidoxorum*; a work on the "primary teachings" of alchemical medicine</note>, *The Metamorphoses*, *The Paramirum* <note>original: *Paramiri*; one of Paracelsus's major medical texts</note>, *On Generations*, and similar works...

This spirit is then **dissolved** in its own, or in common pure water; after this, one separates the pure part from the impure part in warmth using **Spirit of Wine**.

### Paragraph Five.
-> Concerning the Secret Remedies <note>original: *De Arcanis*; the term "Arcanum" refers to a hidden, powerful medicinal virtue or "secret" within a substance</note> of Theophrastus Paracelsus. <-

If one or another seeker of the alchemical art asks what Theophrastus [Paracelsus] intended to be understood by these **Secret Remedies**, let this serve as certain information: they are nothing other than a purified **fifth essence** <note>original: *quinta Essentia*; the most spiritual and potent extract of a substance, beyond the four elements</note>, a purified **mastery** <note>original: *Magisterium*; a preparation that captures the full medicinal power of a substance without separating its elements</note>, or a **first being** <note>original: *erstes Wesen* or *Primum Ens*</note>. Under the **Secret of the First Matter**, however, he means the **First Matter** <note>original: *primam Materiam*</note> itself, or the **First Being of the Human Limbo** <note>original: *primum Ens Limbi humani*; in Paracelsian thought, the "Limbus" is the primordial "great mystery" or "mother" from which the human form was created</note>; likewise, the **First Matter of the Mercury of Salt**, because it is most closely similar to it. Therefore, one should first reduce it back into a liquid substance according to the process of the First Being, and then reunite it with the **Sovereign Principle** <note>original: *Monarchia*; the ruling vital force or essential nature of the substance</note>—as the living, unreduced body of that thing—and bring it to distillation.

As for what is meant by the **Secret of the Stone**, such a thing is better explained in the following practical instructions; for under the **Mercury of Life** <note>original: *Mercurius Vitae*; usually referring to a preparation of antimony, but here used philosophically</note>, the **living fire** itself is indicated. This means that common mercury is turned into an essence with the **Fifth Essence of Salt** and made alive with the **First Being of Antimony** <note>original: *primo Ente Antimonii*</note>, as the heavenly life. The **Secret of the Tincture**, on the other hand, explains itself within the writings themselves, and therefore requires no further explanation here.

# Paragraphus Quintus.
## Concerning the Secrets of Theophrastus Paracelsus.

If any student of the arts is curious to know what **Theophrastus Paracelsus** <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), the Swiss physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of chemicals and minerals in medicine</note> intended to be understood by the term **Secrets** <note>original: *Arcanis*; in Paracelsian medicine, an "Arcanum" is a secret, incorporeal virtue or power within a substance that can heal the body</note>, let this serve as reliable information: such things are nothing other than a **potentiated Fifth Essence** <note>original: *gradirte quinta Essentia*; the "Fifth Essence" or quintessence is the purest, most concentrated part of a substance, and "potentiated" or "graduated" means its medicinal strength has been heightened</note>, a potentiated **Mastery** <term>Magisterium: a finished medicinal preparation where the virtues of a substance are extracted without removing its elemental form</term>, or a **First Being** <note>original: *erstes Wesen* or *primum Ens*; the primordial, underlying vitality of a substance</note>.

Under the first "Secret of the First Matter" <note>original: *Arcano primae Materiae*</note>, however, he intends to be understood the **First Matter** itself, or the **First Being of the Human Limbo** <note>original: *primum Ens Limbi humani*; in Paracelsian theory, the "Limbo" is the primordial "chaos" or reservoir from which the human body was created</note>; likewise, the First Matter of the **Mercury of Salt**, because it is most closely uniform with the human limbo. Therefore, one should first return these substances to a fluid state according to the process of the First Being, and then reunite them with the **Monarchy** <note>original: *Monarchia*; likely referring to the governing vital power or the "ruling" chemical state of the medicine</note>, as the living **unreduced body** <note>original: *Corpore irreducto*; a substance that has not been broken down into its dead, inert components</note> of that thing, and finally bring it to distillation.

As for what is meant by the **Secret of the Stone**, this will be better explained in the following practical section; for under the **Mercury of Life** <note>original: *Mercurius Vitae*; usually referring to a preparation of antimony, but here used to describe a vitalizing agent</note>, the **living fire** itself is indicated. This occurs such that common Mercury is **essencified** <note>refined into its essential state</note> with the Fifth Essence of Salt and made alive with the **First Being of Antimony** <note>original: *primo Ente Antimonii*</note>, as the heavenly life. The **Secret of the Tincture**, on the other hand, is explained within the writings themselves, and therefore requires no further explanation here.

### Paragraph Eight.

### On the Great Composite of the Mysteries of Theophrastus, and in Medicine, the Greatest. <note>original: *De Compoſito Myſteriorum Theophrasti magno, in Medicina autem maximo*</note>

In the **Paramiric Writings** <term>Paramiriſchen Schrifften</term> <note>The *Opus Paramirum*, a major work by Paracelsus (Theophrastus) concerning the causes of disease</note> it is revealed and explained clearly enough for what is necessary for the philosopher and physician: that as far as the entire human body is concerned—not only in its physical-earthly mass, but also in its heavenly-balsamic part—it must be preserved, maintained, and cured of all diseases, both heavenly and earthly. To achieve this, a medicine must be attributed with a specific composition. This composition does not consist merely of a number of separate parts—as when one mixes water and wine together, imagining it to be a true mixture when it is not, since one part can easily be separated from the other without damaging the other part. This [separation] does not happen in our great composition. Instead, a harmonious, pure mixing occurs there, and indeed in such a way that two become one in nature and property. Because of their incomparable **Concordance** <note>original: *Concordanz*; a state of perfect harmony or agreement between substances</note>, they cannot be separated or divided without damage, just like the union of male and female seeds.

Now, if such a composition—which is to be prepared to match man in every proportion of the heavenly and earthly—is to be made, then the name **Microcosm** <term>Microcoſmus</term> <note>The "Little World"—the alchemical concept that the human body is a miniature reflection of the universe</note>, meaning that man is the small world, must be considered; therefore, so far as

# On the Universal or Particular Stone.
## According to Theophrastus Paracelsus,

Who found our matter in Hungary, or in the mountains thirteen miles from Salzburg near Gastein, where the ruined gold mine and the cave or pit there is called the "Red Wall" <note>original: *die rothe Wand*</note>; wherein one finds—most especially in the balsamic months of May, June, and July—a sticky matter hanging from the rocks above, like a thick pitch or resin, or like the gum found on trees, and red like a ruby. This ruby-red matter is scraped off with a silver instrument or spoon, which becomes gilded <note>covered in gold</note> during the scraping and smells like a violet.

The drops, however, which fall down to the ground, are green and just as good as the red ones above: and if one can obtain only a pound of such, one has enough for the work. This thick slime gilds a silver vessel through and through and also dissolves it.

2. Take as much of this slime as can be had, place it in a tall flask, and pour over it a hand-breadth of highly rectified <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: *Spiritum Vini*; concentrated alcohol used as a solvent</note>, as described before, and gradually extract the <term>Green Lion</term> <note>original: *grünen Löwen*; a famous alchemical symbol representing a potent mineral acid or a "raw" solvent capable of dissolving gold</note>. Afterwards, draw off the <term>Menstruum</term> <note>original: *Menstruum*; a solvent used to extract the essence from a solid</note> again with gentle heat. ### Note Well <note>original: "Notandum"</note>

If one can obtain such an earth which, upon glowing <note>The process of heating a substance to a high temperature to observe color changes or drive off impurities.</note>, gives its proper color and remains behind in color like a red minium <note>A bright red pigment, traditionally associated with lead or mercury oxides.</note>, as previously mentioned, then it is correct and suitable. However, if it remains behind as a bluish-red, then such earth is **Martial** <term>Martialisch</term> <note>Alchemical term for substances containing iron, named after Mars.</note>, and not much can be accomplished with its **Spirit** <term>Spiritu</term>. The correct earth must carry a **Solar or Lunar Spirit** <term>Spiritum Solarem vel lunarem</term> <note>Gold-like or silver-like essence.</note> with it; therefore, if one intends to bring a **volatile spirit of salt** <term>Spiritum salis volatilem</term> from such earth, and from the **dead head** <term>Capite mortuo</term> <note>The solid residue left in the distilling vessel after all volatile components have been driven off.</note> bring the **fixed salt** <term>Sal fixum</term> and the **volatile salt** <term>Sal volatile</term> into an oil, one must place it in a **retort** <term>Retort</term> <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation.</note>, pour the Spirit over it, and distill it over by **cohobation** <term>cohobando</term> <note>The repetitive process of pouring a distillate back onto its residue and re-distilling to concentrate the essence.</note>, through which a **separation** <term>Separation</term> then occurs.

To make the ores grow in such a way that the **Soul** <term>Anima</term> can rise to the top, one can only **separate** <term>separiren</term> the aforementioned Spirit from the oil, and pour it onto the Salt which has been extracted **from the dead head** <term>ex Capite mortuo</term>, and distill it over together <note>original: "una cum"</note> by cohobation, whereupon such a **liquid** <term>Liquor</term> can then be used with profit. These clay-like earths are found in gold and silver mines, where such ores grow between the stones, and it is a yellowish-vitriolic earth.

## Procedure for working with this Liquor.

*Take <note>original: "℞," the symbol for Recipe</note> one part of the finest gold, or Calx of Gold <term>Calx Auri: a fine powder produced by heating gold until it loses its metallic form</term>, and ten parts of our Liquor: Let it stand for three hours in a vial <term>Phiola: a small glass vessel</term>; in this way the Seed or Soul is extracted, and at the bottom remains the white Body, from which the Menstruum <term>Menstruum: a powerful alchemical solvent</term> impregnated with the Essence of Gold is separated, and it is placed in the ashes <note>original: "Cineribus," referring to a warm ash bath used to provide gentle, even heat</note>. Then, through ordinary Digestion, it will take on a black, white, lemon-yellow, and finally a deep red color, and it will be coagulated into a Powder or Tincture <term>Tinctura: a potent substance believed to be capable of "tinging" or transforming other materials</term>.*

*To this Powder or Tincture add three parts of our Liquor, and coagulate it as before; and by observing this method, Multiplication occurs infinitely, and the more it is multiplied, the more the Tincture is imbued with power in both Quantity and Quality. Cast some of this Powder upon Mercury <term>Mercurius: quicksilver</term> or another imperfect metal, and it will thus be transformed into the most perfect Gold.*

*Take one grain of this Tincture and ten grains of our aforementioned Liquor, the Alkahest <term>Alkahest: a legendary universal solvent capable of dissolving any substance</term>; let them be distilled together through a retort <term>Retorta: a glass vessel with a long, curved neck</term>, and thus a deep red liquor will immediately pass over, which is the truest Potable Gold <term>Aurum potabile: "drinkable gold," a precious medicinal cordial sought by alchemists</term>. Of which, if the smallest drop is taken every day, the sick person is freed from every disease, and a long life is obtained.*

### Another such Mineral or Earth, as was previously mentioned in the notes, is found in various places; it appears black, adorned with little white stars.

To putrefy <term>putrificiren: the alchemical stage of decomposition and "blackness" (nigredo) necessary for transformation</term> this our philosophical Subject or Matter, two strong flasks <term>Kolben</term> must be sealed together with lute <term>lutirt: sealed with a clay-like cement to make the connection airtight</term>. This matter in the flask is so strong that it is prone to crack the upper flask, indicating that the Mercury seeks to return to its Chaos or Center <note>the "Chaos" refers to the primordial, unformed state of matter</note> in no simple manner. Therefore, for the philosophical resolution <term>Resolution: the process of breaking a solid down into its constituent parts</term>, the glass must be 12 parts empty and filled with only one part of the matter. In contrast, ordinary digestion requires the vessel to be only 2 parts empty and one part full.

When a lead-glance <term>Bley-Glanz: the primary mineral ore of lead, also known as galena, valued for its silver content</term>, which is how our starting material <term>Subiectum: the raw substance chosen for the alchemical process</term> must appear, has a beautiful and high luster, along with beautiful blue and smooth facets where something yellow, red, or brown shows through, then such an ore <term>Minera: raw mineral or ore as it is taken from the earth</term> is good and rich in mercury <term>Mercurio: here referring to the "mercury of the philosophers," the vital, liquid essence within the metal</term>. The best ore is found where lead, silver, and gold are mined; this is black and glass-shiny, and in its hardness it is equal to a mineral of antimony <term>Minerae Antimonii: stibnite, an ore often used as a "purifier" in alchemical work</term>. Other colors of such ores that lie near lead and gold are also not to be excluded, provided they are still immature <term>immatur: minerals believed to be still "growing" in the earth and not yet "ripened" into gold</term> and not yet determined <term>determiniret: fixed into a specific chemical identity or final metallic form</term> to anything, and also lie not far from the lead and gold veins.

Likewise, one is found which is not unlike litharge <term>Silberglätt: a lead oxide formed during the refining of silver</term>, yet is somewhat more glassy. **NB.** When a lead-glance is brittle, beautifully high-glossy, and blue, then it is embryonic <term>embryonirt: existing in an early, undeveloped state containing the "seed" of the work</term> and fit for the Art; therefore, all immature ores <term>Minerae immaturae</term> are not to be excluded, provided they are embryonic. *And this is well to be noted:* That if the first gum <term>Gumma: a resinous or sticky substance produced during the early stages of mineral breakdown</term> is not sufficiently digested <term>digerirt: heated gently and steadily to promote chemical change</term> and thereby dissolved <term>soluiret</term>, one will hardly obtain the spirit of the Azoth <term>Spiritum des Azots: a transformative, universal solvent or "soul" of the matter</term> or vinegar from it. Instead, it will clump together in the flask because it is of a styptic nature <note>original: "stipticae naturae," meaning an astringent or contracting quality that resists being broken down</note>. If one attempts to drive it with force, however, it will fulminate <term>fulminiret: to explode or detonate violently</term>, for which the cause is too little digestion. For all styptics <term>Stiptica: substances with a contracting, binding effect</term>, such as this mineral, when they are sufficiently saturated <term>saturiret</term> with the subtle spirits of the Azoth, let their parts separate from one another and are then ready to be carried over the helm <term>Helm: the top part of a still or alembic where vapors collect</term>. In the absence of such digestion and solution <term>Solution</term>, however, they explode. Therefore, the main point lies in this: that a burning and animated spirit <term>Spiritus ardens et Animatus: a potent, volatile essence believed to be "alive" with transformative power</term> be extracted from the mineral, with which both the ferments <term>Fermenta: substances added to "leaven" or trigger a specific transformation</term> and the mineral's own salt <term>Sal</term> may be fundamentally dissolved. This is then the hidden principle of solution and coagulation <term>Principium Solutionis et Coagulationis: the core alchemical cycle of "dissolve and thicken"</term>, which is known only to the Adepts <term>Adeptis: those who have mastered the "Great Work" of alchemy</term> and to no one else.

If one wishes, however, to proceed according to the process <note>original: "procedere"</note> of the famous Christian Friedrich Sendivogius <note>The text refers to "Sendimiro," likely a variation of Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636), a world-renowned alchemist whose works on "The New Chemical Light" were central to 17th-century science.</note>, then take the previously and so frequently described ore <term>Minerae: raw mineral ore</term> or marcasite <term>Marcasit: a mineral often confused with pyrite, used here as a source of sulfur</term> as you please. Pulverize it as freshly as possible into the finest powder and place it into a well-coated retort <term>Retort: a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling liquids</term>. Let it stand for a time in a damp place, then distill the spirit <term>Spiritum: the volatile, gaseous, or liquid essence of a substance</term> by degrees of fire <note>original: "per Ignis Gradum"</note> over into a well-connected receiver <term>Recipienten: the glass jar that catches the liquid dripping from the retort</term> until no more spirit or vapor wishes to come over. Then let everything cool and grind the remaining body <term>Corpus: the solid material left behind after distillation</term> very delicately. Pour the liquid that came over back onto it, let it soften and soak through well, and distill the spirit from it again while sealed <note>original: "clauſe"</note>. Repeat this three to four times.

Finally, however, rectify <term>rectificire: to purify a liquid by distilling it again, often multiple times</term> the spirit by itself, and calcine <term>calcinire: to heat a solid to high temperatures in order to drive off volatile parts or reduce it to ash</term> the remaining earth for a time until it begins to turn red. As soon as it has become cold, pulverize it finely and pour the spirit of wine <term>Spiritus Vini: high-proof alcohol, used as a powerful solvent</term> described at the beginning of this treatise over it to the height of three or four fingers. Digest <term>digerire: to soak a substance in a solvent under gentle, consistent heat</term> and extract the red color in a flask with gentle heat <note>original: "leni Calore"</note>. Repeat this as often as necessary until the spirit is no longer colored. Pour the collected solution into a flask and draw off <note>original: "abstrahire"</note> the spirit. On the other hand, repeatedly dissolve the sulfur remaining at the bottom <note>original: "in Fundo"</note> with the spirit of wine that was driven off, and separate the dregs <note>original: "Feces"</note> which remain behind with each solution. At last, the spirit will no longer allow itself to be separated; at that point, the sulfur is rightly prepared.

The remaining earth from which the soul <note>In alchemy, "sulfur" was often called the "soul" of the metal, while "mercury" was the "spirit" and "salt" was the "body."</note> has been drawn should be calcined. From it, leach out the body of the moon <note>original: "Corpus Lunae." In this context, it refers to the "salt" or the crystalline essence of the silver/lead material.</note> or of salt, which must be sought and extracted with its own water or spirit. With this, dissolve and purify it, and indeed do this so often and so long until it no longer wishes to crystallize <note>original: "anschiessen"</note> but remains in the glass in the form of an oil. Then it is also well and rightly made.

<margin>✱</margin> Take one part of this refined gold or silver powder, and between 50 to nearly 100 parts of well-purified liquid mercury <term>Mercurio viuo: literally "living mercury," referring to common quicksilver</term> or silver. Let it stand for 6 to 8 hours in a constant flux or heat, and you will see, upon pouring it out, what effect this has within it. Pour off the nitric acid <note>original: "Aquam fortem"</note> and wash the gold calx thoroughly. Reduce it back to metal with borax <term>Borrax: a flux used to aid the melting and purification of metals</term>, and you will find God's blessing <note>A common alchemical euphemism for the successful production of gold.</note> upon pouring it out. The silver, on the other hand, should be precipitated from the nitric acid using copper, with much warm water poured over it—specifically 8 parts water to 1 part nitric acid. Then, wash the silver calx <term>Silber-Kalck: the silver powder recovered from the acid solution</term> that has fallen to the bottom well with clean, warm water and reduce it likewise in the usual manner <note>original: "communi modo"</note> with potash <term>Bodaschen: an alkaline salt used in smelting</term>, so that nothing is lost.

**Metallic Transmutation** <note>original: "Transmutationem Metallicam"</note>, the art of demonstrating how to transform mercury and other imperfect metals along with their ferments into gold and silver, is here set forth quite demonstrably, and shall first be revealed according to **Paracelsus**, as follows:

This distillation must be performed a full 30 times, and indeed as often as necessary until half of the **Water of Life** has vanished. Thus one obtains a red-colored oil; pour this off cleanly and distill it over with a strong fire through a retort, and it will become redder and clearer. This is then called, and truly is, the **Mercury of the Philosophers** in the **Form of Oil**.

### Concluding Note.

There is also found, as mentioned in the notes above, an **Antimony ore** <term>Minera Antimonii</term> of a solar nature, with yellow-blue streaks or otherwise beautiful colors, in Hungary; it possesses extraordinary powers over both humans and metals, and is the most excellent substance after the true, undetermined **Universal Matter** <note>The "Prima Materia" or first matter from which all things in the mineral kingdom originate.</note> of the mineral kingdom. For this reason, it was placed upon the **Triumphal Chariot** by **Basilius Valentinus** <note>Basil Valentine, a legendary 15th-century alchemist (likely a pseudonym) famous for his work on antimony titled *The Triumphal Chariot of Antimony*.</note>. Distill it very gently until it reaches an oily consistency, or until only half has passed over; **cohobate** <term>cohobire</term> <note>A process of repeatedly distilling a liquid by pouring the distillate back onto the solid residue remaining in the flask.</note>, or pour this distilled spirit back onto the remai- <note>The catchword "nent" suggests the word "remanent," referring to the residue left in the flask.</note>

## On the Emerald’s Virtue and Effect.

This stone matures over the course of 500 years, and if it is not found within this time in its "house"—the place where it was **coagulated** <term>coagulirt</term> <note>The alchemical process of a liquid or vapor hardening into a solid stone</note>—it returns again to its **chaos** <term>Chaos</term> or **nothingness** <term>nihilum</term> <note>original: "chaos oder nihilum"; in alchemy, this refers to the formless, original state of matter</note>. **Fifthly**, a chaste, pious, and God-fearing person should always carry this stone with them; thus they will experience the wonders of what virtue it contains, for whatever luck or misfortune is to befall them will appear to them in their sleep.

# Of the Emerald's Virtue and Effect.

This stone is matured over the course of 500 years, and if it is not found within its "house"—the place where it was solidified <term>coagulirt</term> <note>In alchemical theory, stones were believed to grow or "ripen" in the earth like plants, solidifying from a liquid or vaporous state</note>—during this time, it returns again into its chaos or **nothingness** <term>nihilum</term> <note>original: "chaos oder nihilum"; the state of primeval matter before it takes form</note>. Other stones do not do this, but must have several hundred years longer. This Emerald now possesses:

**Firstly**, this virtue: that if it is authentic <note>The author uses "gerecht" (righteous), meaning the stone is genuine and has been properly prepared</note> and is worn by a man or a woman, it will burst asunder if one or the other should be unchaste.

**Secondly**: And if a person conducts themselves temperately and also wears the stone around the neck—provided it has been heated for a quarter of an hour with our **sulfur** <term>Schwefel</term> <note>In alchemy, "sulfur" refers to the active, solar principle of a substance</note> during the **hour of Mercury** <term>hora Mercurii</term> <note>original: "hora Mercurii"; the specific time of day governed by Mercury, believed to influence the mind and communication</note> at the full moon, and has been set into its gold during that same hour—then they shall receive and experience wonderful visions in their sleep.

**Thirdly**: When this stone is purified <term>rectificiret</term> with its sulfur during the **hour of Jupiter** <term>hora Jouis</term> <note>original: "hora Jouis"; the planetary hour associated with growth and protection</note> at the new moon, and is placed into a beaker of wine that contains poison, the wine therein will bubble up as if it were boiling over a fire.

**Fourthly**: An authentic emerald loses its natural color in the presence of unchaste women; however, this can be restored by our sulfur. And if it is worn on the finger or on the body, it strengthens a person uncommonly well.

**Fifthly**: A chaste, pious, and God-fearing person should always carry this stone with them, for they will experience wonders regarding the virtues it contains; for whatever fortune or misfortune is to befall them will appear to them in their sleep.

<meta>This page follows the instructions for the "First Step" of the alchemical process, which involved the sublimation of mercury using vitriol and salt. ### Second Step.
<note>original: "Gradus secundus."</note>

**Take:** Pure tin, one pound, and let it flow in a clean crucible. Then, into the melted tin, stir with a wooden spatula one pound of **living mercury** <term>Mercurium vivum</term> <note>original: "Mercurium vivum"; liquid quicksilver</note> that has been pressed through leather. As soon as the quicksilver begins to sputter or smoke, take the crucible from the fire and pour the material into cold water. It will then become brittle and as crumbly as a dough. 

Grind this dough, or **amalgam** <term>Amalgama</term> <note>An alloy of mercury with another metal—in this case, tin—which creates a pasty consistency</note>, in an iron mortar with strong wine-vinegar and salt poured over it until it is very fine. When it is well ground, pour off the vinegar and add warm water; grind it again, repeatedly pouring off and adding warm water, until no more blackness comes from it. Finally, it can be ground with cold water alone. 

Continue this grinding or amalgamating for 8 or 9 days, and do not cease until the **amalgam** has become completely pure, as clear as a mirror, snow-white, and as soft as butter. Then, grind it on a stone with an equal weight of the **sublimated mercury** <term>Mercurii sublimati</term> <note>The purified mercury produced in the first step of this work</note> prepared above. While doing so, saturate it with the **vitriol water** <term>Vitriol-Wasser</term> <note>An acidic liquid distilled from vitriol</note> that was driven over from the **sublimated mercury**. Grind everything well together and afterward place it on a glass plate in a damp cellar. Place a glass vessel underneath and catch the **sublimated mercury** as it runs down into it like milk. In this way, within 14 days, one will obtain the oil or milk of mercury.

The **dregs** <term>Feces</term> <note>original: "Feces"; the solid residue remaining on the plate</note> which remain on the plate, however, should be stirred well with a wooden spatula and left to lie until no more milk flows from them. Then, seal the oil in a flask fitted with a **blind helm** <note>original: "blinden Helme"; a still-head without a spout, used for refluxing where vapors return to the flask instead of being collected</note> and place it for 4 weeks in a **water bath** <term>Balneum Mariae</term> <note>A vessel of hot water used for gentle, uniform heating</note> for **putrefaction** <term>Putrefaction</term> <note>A stage of chemical breakdown or "rotting" often associated with a change in the substance's color and consistency</note>. After the 4 weeks have passed, open the flask, **seal** <note>original: "lutire"; to seal the joints with an airtight clay or paste</note> an open helm onto it, and distill the oil over into a well-attached **receiver** <term>Recipienten</term> using a very gentle degree of fire.

## Sixth Grade.

### Gradus sextus.

Take <margin>Take.</margin> pure tin, as much as you like, burn and calcine <note>To calcine is to reduce a metal to a powder (oxide) through prolonged heating.</note> it well in a new pot; reduce and melt it with saltpeter and tree oil <note>original German: "Baumöl," usually referring to olive oil or a similar high-quality vegetable oil.</note> as follows: Rub everything well together until it becomes like a dough, then place it in a crucible, set it in a wind-furnace, and blow strongly until it is brought into a flow; once it has flowed well, pour it into a mold to form a regulus <term>König</term> <note>The 'king' or metallic button that settles at the bottom of a crucible after smelting.</note>; calcine this regulus again just as the first time, and reduce it again with saltpeter <term>Nitro</term> and tree oil, as was done above. ## Seventh Grade.

### Gradus septimus.

->In which the spirit is joined with the body<-

Next, distill the water over the helm, and a portion of the water will immediately turn into oil. Add another portion of the earth <note>the solid residue</note> into the distilled water, dissolve it, and continue to distill it together; it will then become oil. This must be done so long and so often until the body has been entirely converted into an oil and has become transparent. This oil cannot be corrupted and awaits its ferment.

### Eighth Grade.

### Gradus octauus. <note>Latin: "Eighth Grade"</note>

<margin>Take.</margin>Take one part of its cemented, thinly beaten, or filed gold, and three parts of minium <term>Mennig</term> <note>Red lead (lead tetroxide), often used in alchemy as a flux or to assist in oxidation.</note> washed with salt and vinegar; make an amalgam <note>A mixture of a metal with mercury; here, it refers to the resulting metallic paste.</note> from this, and wash it afterward with salt and pure spring water; then soak it with the oil described above, close it in a vial, place it for one month in the heat of the ashes <note>A method of gentle, indirect heating where the vessel is buried in warm ashes.</note>, and stir it every day until it has become a powder and looks as black as a raven <note>original: "schwartz als ein Raabe"; this is the 'Nigredo' stage, symbolizing the death or dissolution of the matter.</note>, which is then the first dissolution <term>Soluirung</term>, and it has a very foul smell. Afterward, grind the powder finely again, moisten it again with its water, put it in its glass, and give it a strong fire for 3 hours, and turn the vial over often; thus it will receive a red color before the yellow, and when it is brought thus far, grind and moisten it again; give it a great fire again for one month, and our mass will truly enter into the red color. Therefore, just continue with the said heat until it is brought into the highest red color and thus has become fire-resistant <note>Stable under high heat without evaporating or changing further.</note>.

This tincture has been kept very secret by the Philosophers <note>Alchemists frequently referred to themselves as "Philosophers."</note> until now, but now it is communicated to the lover [of the art], and consists solely in our Oil of Mercury <term>Oil of Mercury</term><note>Latin: Oleo Mercurii; a purified, liquid form of mercury considered essential for the Great Work.</note> with its ferment <term>ferment</term><note>Latin: Fermento; an agent added to a substance to trigger its transformation into gold or silver.</note>.

NB. The quantity <term>quantity</term><note>Latin: Quantum.</note> of the tincture to be added is indeed not specified here, but the lover of the art will surely find the correct weight, provided he obtains the tincture. For if he should add too much of the tincture during the tinging <note>The process of "coloring" or transforming a base metal into a noble one.</note>, and make the metal more than perfect <term>more than perfect</term><note>Latin: plusquam perfect; a state where the metal is refined to such a high degree that it can act as a catalyst for further transmutations.</note>, he will already know how to help himself. Praise God!

### Note: <note>Latin: Notandum.</note>

->How the tin—belonging to the above sixth degree—as well as<-
->the lead is to be calcined, occurs in the following manner,<-
->namely:<-

Dissolve it in strong water <term>strong water</term><note>Latin: Aqua forti; nitric acid, commonly used by alchemists to dissolve and separate metals.</note> into a lime <note>A powder or ash resulting from the process of calcination.</note>, wash it well until it is sweet, and use it as required above. Or: Calcine it by stirring <term>stirring</term><note>Latin: agitando.</note> on a shard with sal ammoniac <term>sal ammoniac</term><note>Latin: Sale Armoniaco; ammonium chloride, used as a flux to help metals melt or react.</note>, or even just with salt. But it is best with the salt which is extracted and prepared from the "dead head" <term>dead head</term><note>Latin: ex Capite mortuo; the solid residue remaining after a substance has been distilled or heated to exhaustion.</note> of Vitriol and strong water; then reverberate <note>To heat a substance in a furnace where the flames are directed or "reverberated" back onto the material.</note> it after the calcination, and thus the tin-lime is rightly prepared. Now there remains only that one also knows how and for what purpose the hours of the day and night are governed by the planets, which will be clearly seen in the tables set down below.

Place it in a cool cellar, and in a few hours, both will turn into a beautiful crystal. ### V.
# Oak Vinegar.
<note>original: "Acetum Quercinum"</note>

<margin>✿</margin> Take **oak wood**, or its **sawdust**, **as much as you wish** <note>original: "q. v." or "quantum vis"</note>. It is just as useful in treating the **French Disease** <note>syphilis</note> as the **spirit of holy wood** <note>original: "Spiritus ex Ligno sancto"; likely referring to Guaiacum wood, a common early modern treatment for syphilis.</note> or **sassafras**, for it powerfully induces sweating, especially if one adds some **fixed mercury** <term>Mercurio fixo</term> or **diaphoretic antimony** <term>Antimonio Diaphoretico</term> to it.

This spirit, taken in water once or three times, cures the **bloody flux** <note>original: "rothe Ruhr"; dysentery.</note> when nothing else will help, especially in children; one can even cook and give small children their porridge with it.

This vinegar heals fresh **flesh wounds** without any stitching and without any other medicine, simply applied warm with a sponge. Likewise, it very quickly heals other **putrid sores**.

For **hollow and rotten toothaches**, take 1 **scruple** <note>A small unit of weight, roughly 1.3 grams.</note> of the **Secret Remedy** in a spoonful of **vinegar** <term>Aceti</term>, and hold it against the teeth; this makes the pains vanish, and it draws out substantial phlegm and the **worms** <note>In this era, it was commonly believed that "tooth worms" were the cause of decay and dental pain.</note>.

In **jaundice**, it serves uncommonly well if one mixes a little **Essence of Saffron** <term>Ess. Croci</term> into it and takes 4 or 5 doses, sweating a little afterward; then help is at hand.

#### Theophrastus’s Specific Purgative.

Filter the clear solution and boil it down to a salt in a wide flask. Glow this salt thoroughly in a crucible for one hour. This must be done a third time, and thus one will obtain a white and clear salt.

### XXII.
### On Salt and its Sweet Crystals.

<margin>♃ <note>This is the symbol for the planet Jupiter. In alchemical practice, it is often associated with the metal tin or specific timing for operations.</note></margin> Take good sea salt, as much as you wish <note>original: *q. v.* or *quantum vis*</note>. When it has settled, add several more drops, and repeat this until all the salt has risen over. Then, let the fire go out and everything cool down. Pour a little wine over it and let it stand overnight, then pour off the wine and give it to the patient; thus it purges very gently and is magnificent for **gouty pains** <note>original: *Doloribus Arthriticis*</note>, joint diseases, **contractures** <term>Contracturen: the shortening and hardening of muscles or tendons, leading to rigid joints.</term>, and the like.

For strong individuals, however, 5 to 8 grains of this cinnabar can be administered in a **purgative extract** <note>original: *Extractu Catharctico*</note>, followed by a drink of wine.

**NB.** Also mentioned during the preservation of the cinnabar and the **butter of antimony** <note>original: *Butter*, referring here to "Butter of Antimony" (antimony trichloride), a thick, oily substance.</note> driven over from it is an oil which, when purified twice, is shiny and gold in color.

### Another [Form of] Mercury of Life.

<margin>Take.</margin> Take the white powder <note>referring to the *Mercurius Vitae* described on the previous page</note> and an equal weight of common cooking salt; rub it upon a stone without ceasing for an entire day. **Aloe** 1 ½ Scruples.

## Preparation of Sweet Mercury.
### Pertaining to the pills mentioned above.

<margin>Recipe.</margin> Take half a pound of the best sublimated mercury <note>original: *Mercurii optime sublimati*; this refers to corrosive sublimate or mercuric chloride.</note> and 6 ounces of liquid mercury <note>quicksilver</note>, purified in the best manner. With these, create an **amalgam** <term>Amalgam: A mixture created by "killing" liquid mercury with another metal or salt until it forms a paste.</term>, and **sublimate** it in a good glass flask with an open helm <term>Helm: The top part of a still or alembic that collects and directs vapors.</term> attached, so that by a graded fire everything rises to the top. Whatever passes over as liquid mercury, cast aside. The **sublimate**, however, should be sublimated again, and this for a 4th or 5th time, so that it becomes as clear as a **crystal** and loses all its **sharpness** <note>The "sharpness" refers to the caustic or corrosive quality of the chemicals; repeating the process made it "sweet" or mild.</note>. Grind this finely, pour **rose water** over it, let it stand for a while, then pour the water off and add more; let it rest again, and once it has been poured off once more, dry the powder very gently. Thus, this is a truly magnificent **purging mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius purgans*</note>. The dose is in proportion to the person; of this, take 15 to 20 **grains**, made into pills with **Cathartic Extract**.

### XXXII.
## The Coral Secret of Theophrastus Paracelsus,

<margin>Recipe.</margin> Take 4 ounces of liquid mercury, purified in the best manner. Dissolve it entirely in the proper **spirit of nitre** <term>Spirit of Nitre: Nitric acid.</term>; boil the solution in a sealed glass vial until the spirit is almost entirely red, and the mercury gradually begins to settle at the bottom, and finally the spirit vanishes entirely, while the mercury appears like a **crystal**. Pulverize this finely, put it in a vial, pour **spirit of nitre** over it again, and boil it in the same manner as before until the spirit has again vanished. Perform this pouring on and thickening <note>original: *inspisiren*</note> for a third time; then it will finally become as **red as a coral**, and **sweet as sugar**.
This is the true **Coral Secret of Paracelsus** <note>original: *Arcanum Corallinum Paracelsi*; chemically, this process produces red mercuric oxide, which was highly valued in alchemy.</note>, with which he performed so many deeds and wonders. Dose: 3, 4, to 5 **grains**.

## XXXIII.
# Universal Balsam.

**Red Myrrh**.

**Juniper oil** and **turpentine oil**.

- - **Amber** [oil] <note>original: *Succini*</note>: 1 ounce.
**Highly rectified spirits of wine**: Half a measure <note>original: *Mens. ß*</note>.

Distill by the **grades of fire** <note>gradually increasing the heat</note> until nothing more will rise over; and keep it for use. For this balsam serves not only for **prevention** but also for **cure**.

## Preparation of Oil of Vitriol.
### For the medicine described above.

<margin>Recipe.</margin>
Take one pound each of the pure crystals, which have been prepared from **native vitriol** <term>Vitriol: A general term for sulfate minerals; "native" means it was sourced directly from the earth.</term>, and **quicklime** <note>original: *lebendigen Kalcks*; calcium oxide, a caustic alkaline substance.</note>. Mix them together well in powdered form and pour pure, warm **rainwater** over them so that everything dissolves completely. Filter the solution and evaporate the filtered liquid until the salt falls to the bottom; then let the half-evaporated liquid sit in the cellar on **juniper twigs** <note>original: *Wacholder-Reisern*</note> to form into crystals. Repeat this described process with the crystals four times. 

Afterward, dissolve these obtained crystals in warm rainwater and **precipitate** <note>original: *praecipitire*; a chemical process where a solid is made to separate from a liquid solution.</note> the solution with **Oil of Antimony** <term>Oil of Antimony: Likely antimony trichloride, a highly corrosive substance used in early chemistry to "purify" other metals.</term>; the corrosive element will gradually settle to the bottom in the form of a white-green powder. On the other hand, very gently pour the clear solution off from the corrosive powder and evaporate it until dry. Redissolve the remaining residue with **rectified Spirit of Wine** <term>Spirit of Wine: High-proof distilled alcohol.</term> and let it crystallize again in a **cold place** <note>original: *Loco frigido*</note>. 

Seal these crystals in a vial and place them in **horse manure** <note>original: *Roß-Mist*; used by alchemists as a natural, steady heat source for gentle digestion.</note> or a **steam bath** <note>original: *Dampf-Baad*</note> for **putrefaction** <term>Putrefaction: In alchemy, a stage of breaking down a substance through gentle heat and moisture until it changes form.</term>, until they have dissolved themselves, which will happen within 14 days. 

Then, distill this oil through a **retort** <note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling liquids.</note> in warm sand. Extract the salt from the **dead head** <term>Caput Mortuum (Dead Head): The useless solid residue remaining in the retort after all volatile liquids have been distilled away.</term> that remained in the retort. Filter and evaporate the solution, which was done with rainwater, and add it to the oil; then it is correct.

### Sylvius’s Volatile Oily Salt.

### XXXVI.
## Dippel’s Styptic Liquor.
<note>original: *Liquor stypticus Dippelii*; Johann Konrad Dippel was a famous 17th-century alchemist and physician. A "styptic" is a substance used to stop bleeding.</note>

Take: Betony herb <note>original: *Herb. Betonic.*</note>
- - Italian Pimpernel or our native Burnet <note>original: *Pimpinell. Italic. vel sangui sorbae nostrat.*</note>
- - Chervil <note>original: *Chaerefol.*</note>
- - Great Houseleek <note>original: *Sedi maior*; literally "Great Stonecrop," often used to cool inflammation.</note>
- - A sufficient quantity of each. <note>original: *aa. q. s.*</note>

Press the juice from these herbs, and
Take: 5 pounds <note>original: *lbv.*</note> of this juice, as well as 5 pounds of strong wine vinegar. Pour these into a glass retort, set a receiver before it, and distill this liquor over by gradual heat <note>original: *per Gradum Ignis*</note>, and preserve it for use.

This styptic liquor stills all bleeding, both internally and externally; it suppresses and drives away gout <note>original: *die Gichter*</note>, obstructions, cramps, and the falling sickness <note>original: *fallende Sucht*; an old term for epilepsy</note>: as well as all sorts of occurring symptoms, when 20, 25, to 30 drops are taken in a suitable carrier liquid <note>original: *Vehiculo*</note>, such as Shepherd's Purse water <note>original: *Aqua Bursae pastoris*</note> and the like.

And if one has injured pulse-veins or arteries <note>original: *Puls- oder Schlag-Adern*</note>, or if an arm or another limb is removed, such a juice stills the bleeding and heals the wounds: which experience has often proven.

### XXXIX.
## Frankfurt Pills.
<note>original: *Pilulae Francofurtenfes*; a well-known 17th-century digestive and laxative formulation.</note>

<margin>Take:</margin> **A**loe, of the best quality and powdered, 1 pound; <note>original: *℔j.*</note> and water in which fresh violets have been soaked three times, 3 pounds; <note>original: *℔iij.*</note> good white wine, 2 pounds. <note>original: *℔ij.*</note>

Dissolve everything over a gentle charcoal fire and filter it through a hair-sieve or a linen cloth; then add to it precipitated and powdered tartar, <note>original: *Tartari praecipitati*; likely cream of tartar used as a purifier.</note> 3 ounces, <note>original: *℥iij.*</note> and boil everything down to the consistency of honey. <note>original: *ad Conſiſtentiam Mellis*</note>

This mass can be kept in bladders or small boxes greased with sweet almond oil, or formed into pills weighing half a grain each. Dosage: 10, 12, to 15 grains.

->Virtue and Use.<-
<note>original: *Virtus et Ufus*</note>

These pills can be taken by old and young persons, as well as by pregnant women. They carry away all phlegm and bile from the stomach, intestines, and the great veins, <note>original: *Grös-Aederlein*; likely referring to the mesenteric veins which were thought to transport humors.</note> along with wind [gas]: they kill worms. One can use them at any time every 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, or 7th day in beer, soup, or tea one hour before dinner; and if they should not open the bowels sufficiently, one can take such a dose again the next day an hour before the midday meal, and even for a third time before dinner.

## LV.
### A Water against Stone, Sand, and Gravel.
<note>In historical medicine, "stone, sand, and gravel" referred to various sizes of kidney and bladder stones.</note>

<margin>Take:</margin> White Sanicle <note>a medicinal herb used for its perceived healing and astringent properties</note>, Lavender blossoms, and field-pigeon dung, 4 handfuls <note>original: *Manip. iv.*</note> of each. High-quality white wine, 1½ measures <note>original: *Menſ. iß.*</note>.

Place this in gentle digestion <term>Digestion: the process of letting ingredients steep in a liquid at a mild, constant warmth to extract their properties</term> for 9 or 10 days, and then distill it over, and sweeten the distillate with candied sugar.

Dosage: One spoonful in the morning and at night. Through this, the phlegmatic stomach is cleansed, and the "urine-wind" <note>likely referring to strangury or painful, difficult urination</note> is driven out. This wine can be used very usefully in all kinds of illnesses and heals everything internally. <margin>Dosage: 2</margin> spoonfuls taken in the morning on an empty stomach. It has driven large stones out of patients, of which *Ioannes Seidel*, Dean at Deutschbrodt <note>now Havlíčkův Brod in the Czech Republic</note> in Bohemia, is a living witness.

### LXIII.
## An excellent face-wash, useful for ladies.

Take: <note>The symbol ♃ is used here as a shorthand for "Recipe," the Latin command to "Take."</note> 1 ounce of yellow sulfur, or flowers of sulfur <note>original: *Flores Sulphuris*; a bright yellow powder produced by sublimating natural sulfur.</note>.
2 ounces of olive oil <note>original: *Baumöl*.</note>.
2 ounces of red myrrh <note>original: *Myrrh. rubr.*</note>.
6 grains of ambergris <note>original: *Ambra*; a rare substance traditionally used in perfumes and medicines.</note>.

Pulverize everything finely and pour one pound of rose water over it in a low-necked flask or retort. Seal a receiving vessel to it <note>original: *lutire einen Recipienten an*; "luting" involved sealing the joints of glass apparatus with clay or paste to prevent vapors from escaping.</note>, and distill everything that will come over in a water bath <term>Balneo Mariae: a gentle heating method where the vessel sits in boiling water rather than over a direct flame.</term>. Then, wash the face with this at night when going to sleep; in the morning, wash yourself clean again with bean-water <note>Water in which beans have been boiled was a common historical skin softener.</note> or spring water, and the face will become beautiful and delicate.

Grind the Cinnabar of Antimony <note>original: *Antimonii*; a red mineral compound of mercury and sulfur associated with antimony</note> on a stone for 2 hours until it is most delicate; do the same with the Native Cinnabar <note>original: *Berg-Zinnober*; naturally occurring mercury sulfide</note>, each separately. Pour one or two spoonfuls of good Rose Water onto the Native Cinnabar and grind it into a small paste or pulp, and let it dry overnight. Thereafter, grind the Cinnabar of Antimony into it as well, and when both are well mixed and ground, grind the sugar into it also, so that everything becomes imperceptible <note>meaning a powder so fine that individual grains cannot be felt</note>. Then drop the Oil of Cinnamon into this powder little by little and mix it well together; it will become quite loose and spongy, and can be kept for use well-sealed in small glass vials.

### Power and Usage <note>original: *Virtus et Usus*</note>

This powder strengthens the head, the kidneys, and all the limbs. It protects a person from strokes <note>original: *Schlage*</note> and dizziness, serves against palpitations of the heart, fainting, and trembling of the limbs, as well as against fatigue; in cases of diarrhea, it acts as a gentle astringent and strengthens the stomach. This powder stills vomiting, warms a chilled stomach, and strengthens it mightily. Likewise, it promotes digestion <note>original: *Concoction*; an archaic medical term for the "cooking" or ripening of humors in the body, particularly during digestion</note>.

In cases of strokes, choking fits <note>original: *Steck-Flüssen*; likely referring to respiratory congestion or sudden catarrh</note>, and paralysis of the tongue, a knife-point’s worth of this powder is sprinkled under the tongue and a little wine is given afterward so that it may be washed down; it immediately brings back the lost speech and encourages the vital spirits <note>original: *Lebens-Geister*; the subtle substances then believed to circulate through the nerves to provide movement and sensation</note>.

This powder serves the elderly and weakened persons especially and uncommonly well, for it strengthens and warms them. For pregnant women, it strengthens the unborn child <note>original: *die Geburt*</note> and prevents miscarriage <note>original: *abordiren*</note>. In the hour of birth, however, both mother and child are strengthened by it, and it helps toward a speedy delivery <note>original: *Beförderung*</note>.

## LXXIII.
## The Miraculous Plaster <note>original: *Emplastrum miraculosum*</note>

| Ingredient | Quantity |
| :--- | :--- |
| <margin>Take <note>original: *℞*</note></margin> Red Lead <note>original: *Minii*</note> | 2 ounces |
| Italian White Lead <note>original: *Cerusae Ital.* or *Bleyweiß*</note> | 2 ounces |
| <term>Olive Oil</term> <note>original: *Olei olivar.* or *Baumöl*; commonly used as a base for ointments</note> | 4 ounces |
| <term>Venetian Soap</term> <note>original: *Sapon. Venet.*; a high-quality soap made from olive oil and soda</note> | 1 ounce |
| <term>Camphor</term> dissolved in Spirit of Wine <note>original: *Camphor. in Spiritu Vini solut.*</note> | 1 ounce |

First, melt the olive oil over a gentle coal fire, then add the finely chopped soap into it; let it cook slowly therein until it begins to become sticky between the fingers. After that, stir the white lead into it bit by bit with a spatula, and take care that it does not overflow; let it continue to cook gently until it starts to thicken. Then add the red lead <note>original: *Menig*</note> also bit by bit and, stirring it over the coals, let it become a dough. Once it has been brought to this point, pour the dissolved camphor into it as well; stir it constantly, and indeed for so long until all the moisture has evaporated.

When this plaster has obtained its consistency, roll or turn it with hands that have been smeared with olive oil into small sticks, and place these into paper that has also been smeared with olive oil, and preserve it for use. Thus applied in the manner of a plaster, it heals all old and fresh wounds in a short time. Now I will make an end to these tested surgical medical remedies with a very unpleasant, yet excellent secret of nature—one which is unbecoming for <term>pharmacists</term> <note>original: *Pharmaceuticis*</note> to prepare because of the very foul odor it causes—through which medicament a lover of surgery...

...as much and even more than an inexperienced <term>physician</term> <note>original: *Medicus*</note> will be able to accomplish, and consists of the following:

### LXXIV.

It is namely a <term>distilled</term> oil, separated from its <term>salt</term>, which is produced <term>from human excrement</term> <note>original: *ex Excrementis Hominis*; this reflects an archaic alchemical practice of distilling organic matter to find a "universal" spirit or essence</note> through <term>retorts</term> <note>glass vessels with long, downward-pointing necks used for distilling liquids</note>, without the addition of any other thing, <term>rectified</term> <note>purified through repeated distillation</note> and cleaned so long and often—occurring at least through the 15th repetition—until it leaves behind no more burnt, black sediment.

This oil, I say, is what, when 30 to 40 drops are taken on an empty stomach before a <term>paroxysm</term> <note>the sudden onset or fit of a disease, such as the shivering fit of a fever</note>, expels all fevers by means of a sweet sleep—which is entirely above suspicion despite some numbing properties—and with which one can also work wonders, so to speak, in other very dangerous conditions. This is well worth noting.

### To Zoilus, however, that poet says:
<note>Zoilus was a historical figure known for his harsh, cynical criticism; in this context, the author is addressing potential critics of his unconventional alchemical remedies.</note>

->Why, envious one, do you tear at the writings of the Chemists with a dog-like snarl? They reveal whatever lies hidden in the world.<-
<note>original: *Rictu, cur laceras Chymicorum scripta, canino, Inuide? quae monstrant, quidquid in orbe latet.*</note>

To the eager lover [of this art], on the other hand, I wish from the dear **God** all blessings for his undertaking, a successful progress in his work, and a prosperous benefit for himself as well as his neighbor, along with the constant health resulting from it; which he shall receive when he prays to Him in spirit and truth. Farewell. <note>original: *Vale*</note>

**Ablution** <note>original: *Abluiren*</note> means: When a thing—be it mineral, animal, or vegetable—is washed clean, or rinsed and purified of its dross, or separated from the mountain-rock and brought to a state of <term>ore concentrate</term> <note>original: *Schlich*; the fine, crushed ore remains after washing away the lighter stony material</note>.

**Abstraction** <note>original: *Abstrahiren*</note> is: When the wateriness or the <term>phlegm</term> <note>the inactive, watery part of a substance</note> is drawn off, driven out, or distilled from the oil—or the spirit from the water and phlegm, or even from the oil—by means of a flask or <term>retort</term> <note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck</note> into another glass or <term>receiver</term> <note>original: *Recipienten*</note> placed before it, heated in a <term>sand bath</term> <note>original: *Sand-Capelle*; a container of sand used to distribute heat evenly around laboratory glassware</note>.

**Agitation** <note>original: *Agitiren*</note> is: When something is shaken and mixed together by moving it in a glass. Or: When one constantly stirs a metal soaked in lead, or a <term>metallic saffron</term> <note>original: *Crocum Metallicum*; a roasted metal oxide, often reddish, used in medicinal and chemical preparations</note> or other prepared matter in which much sulfur and other dross still clings, using an iron wire or a "little crutch" <note>a small stirring tool</note> so that it does not burn, and so that it refines well <note>original: *einseigere*; a metallurgical term for refining by melting</note> and does not fuse together, allowing the antimonial or other sulfur within it to be smoked out and driven away.

**Amalgamation** <note>original: *Amalgamiren*</note> means this much: When one rubs gold, silver, lead, or a <term>Martial regulus of antimony</term> <note>original: *Regulum Antimonii Martialem*; a metallic form of antimony produced by refining it with iron ("Mars")</note> and the like with mercury to form a mass or dough-like paste in a glass, stone, or iron mortar.

**Cohobating, or repeating by cohobation** <note>original: *per Cohobia repetiren*</note>, means this: that when one wishes to increase the power and strength of a spirit <note>a volatile substance or distillate</note> or an oil, one frequently drives it over or distills it from the remaining mass or matter, then pours the distillate back onto the matter and drives it over again. This must often be done 3, 4, 5, or even up to 6 times. This is called cohobating. For this, one requires sand-baths <note>vessels filled with sand to provide even, indirect heat</note>, distillation furnaces, flask-glasses, and retorts, along with receivers and good lutes <note>pastes used to seal the joints of the glassware</note>.

**Conjoining means:** When one unites one spirit or oil with another—specifically in glass vessels using gentle heat—or joins gold and silver through melting. It also refers to the putting together and binding of the spirit, body, and soul—that is, Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury <note>original: *Sal, Sulphur et Mercurium*; the three primary components of all matter in alchemical theory</note>—in our philosophical works.

**Corrupting is:** When one burns a substance—be it a metal or mineral—with sulfur, or eats it away, dissolves it, and destroys it with corrosive waters <note>strong acids</note>; or perhaps when one precipitates a mixed spirit, oil, or similar substance using a salt, vitriol <note>sulfate minerals</note>, or antimonial oil, and thus separates them from one another again.

One then filters the extract and evaporates the filtered liquid in glass or other vessels until it is reduced by half, or until a thin skin is seen upon the moisture. The evaporated liquid is then placed in a cool cellar for several days to let the crystals "shoot" <note>precipitate out of the solution</note> or grow. **To extract** <note>original: *Extrahiren*</note> means: When one draws out the power, quintessence, soul <note>original: *animam*</note>, or sulfur <note>in alchemy, "sulfur" often refers to the oily, combustible, or active principle of a substance</note> from an already decomposed body using a solvent <note>original: *menstruo*</note>, such as spirit of wine <note>high-proof alcohol</note>, vinegar, an alkahest <note>a theoretical universal solvent</note>, and the like: for which glass flasks, filters, and digestion ovens are necessary.

**To filter** <note>original: *Filtriren*</note> is this: If one intends to separate various waters, spirits, tinctures, or oils—which are impure and cloudy—from their earthiness <note>original: *Terrestrität*; solid sediment</note>, or also wishes to purify a dissolved salt-water and similar extractions, this must be done through gray paper or a Hippocras bag <note>a conical filter bag</note> made of thick felt, through which one lets such liquids run, or also through a tenaculum <note>original: *Tenackel*; a wooden frame used to hold a straining cloth taut</note> of stretched thick cloth, and through glass and other funnels.

**To Extract** <term>Extrahiren</term> means: When one draws out the power, **quintessence**, **soul** <note>original Latin: *Animam*</note>, or the **sulfur** from an already decomposed body using a **solvent** <term>Menstruo</term>, such as **spirit of wine** <note>original Latin: *Spiritu Vini*; a high-proof alcohol</note>, vinegar, an **alkahest** <note>a theoretical universal solvent capable of dissolving every other substance</note>, and the like. **To Ferment** <term>Fermentiren</term> is: When one adds a **ferment** of gold, silver, or another metal and mineral to a matter or a **tincture**, in order to make it **more than perfect** <note>original Latin: *plusquam perfect*</note>, letting it **digest** <note>to heat a substance gently to encourage chemical change</note> for its allotted time, and then **reduces** it again and brings it to a pure state.

**To Fix** <term>Figiren</term> is: When one makes **mercury**, a **philosophical tincture**, or other incomplete matter fire-resistant or **capable of withstanding the cupel** <note>original: *Capellen-haltig*; referring to the cupellation process where metals are tested by extreme heat</note> by pouring over them reliable **solvents**, **spirits**, or **oils**, followed by **digesting** and **distilling** <term>abstrahiren</term>. Likewise: When one makes a volatile and soft matter hard and durable so that it does not soften in the fire. For this, **glass flasks**, but commonly **vials** <term>Phiolen</term>—which must be well-sealed—are required.

**To Filter** <term>Filtriren</term> is this: If one intends to separate various waters, **spirits**, **tinctures**, or **oils**—which are impure and cloudy—from their **earthiness** <note>original: *Terrestrität*; the solid dross or sediment</note>, or if one wishes to purify a dissolved salt-water and similar **extractions**, this must be done through gray paper or a **Hippocras-bag** <note>original: *Hipocras-Sack*; a conical fabric filter named after the physician Hippocrates</note> made of thick felt, through which one lets the liquid run; or also through a **strainer-frame** <term>Tenackel</term> of stretched thick cloth, and through glass and other **funnels**.

**To Imbibe** <term>Imbibiren</term> means: When one wishes to saturate a **tincture** and bring it to a **perfect state**, as well as to increase it. For this purpose, one pours in its specific **dose** <term>Dofin</term> or portion of the already prepared **oil**, **spirit**, or **alkahest** <note>a universal solvent</note>—as **Theophrastus** <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), a pioneer of the medical revolution of the Renaissance</note> calls it. **To Inspissate** <term>Inſpiſſiren</term> is: When one dries out a moist matter until it reaches its proper consistency; this is achieved through a mild **digestion** <note>slow, steady heating in a controlled environment</note>.

**To Irrigate** <term>Irroriren</term> has this meaning: When one moistens a prepared dry powder with a **spirit** or **oil**, with a **vinegar** or another suitable water, much like a **dew**. This makes it similar to a **pulpy mass** <note>original Latin: *Massa pulpae*</note>, which is then dried again in mild heat. This process is repeated several times.
