**To Laminate** <term>Laminiren</term> is: When one beats gold or silver and similar metals into thin sheets, so that one can subsequently dissolve them in **Royal Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua Regis*; a powerful mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold</note>, **Strong Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua forti*; nitric acid</note>, and similar **corrosive spirits** <note>original Latin: *Spiritibus corrosiuis*</note>, or can **cement** <term>cementiren</term> <note>a process where metal is surrounded by powdered chemicals and heated to purify it or change its properties</note> them with other minerals and materials.

**To Alloy** <term>Legiren</term> is: When one mixes silver, copper, or other metal into gold, or copper and lesser metals into silver, and melts them together, so that it becomes higher in the assay, or lower according to the internal value; for which crucibles, fluxing powders, and **ingot molds** <term>Inguß</term> are required.

**To Liquefy** <term>Liquesciren</term>, or melt is: When one allows a metal or mineral to enter into flux and flow well in a crucible before a bellows or in a wind furnace: for which likewise good crucibles, as well as necessary fluxing powders, **ingot molds**, **casting cones** <term>Gieß-Puckel</term> <note>a conical iron mold used to collect molten metal so that the heavier metal settles at the bottom, separate from the slag</note>, and the like are required.

**To Lute** <term>Lutiren</term> is: When one drives distilled and sharp spirits from a flask or **retorts** <term>Retorten</term> into a **receiver** <term>Recipienten</term> or **collection glass** <term>Vorlage-Glaß</term>, one must place good plasters <note>sealants or adhesives used to make joints airtight</note>, which hold back the **spirits**, around the joints; or if one wishes to **cement**, a fire-resistant ointment must likewise be placed around the joints of the **cementing boxes**, and, so that in an open fire a glass **retort** or **flask** does not tear in two or crack, such a vessel must be coated with good clay <note>this protective coating was called "lorication"</note>.

**To Multiply** <term>Multipliciren</term> is: When one increases and improves a **tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> <note>the alchemical catalyst or "Philosopher's Stone" used to transform base metals into gold</note> in such a manner and thus in its power and **quality and quantity** <note>original Latin: *Quali- et Quantitate*</note>, whereby one can subsequently obtain more gold and silver from the imperfect metals or other materials and minerals.

**To Precipitate** <term>Praecipitiren</term> means: When gold dissolved in **Royal Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua Regis*; a powerful mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids</note> or silver dissolved in **Strong Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua forti*; nitric acid</note> is made to fall and is struck down into a **calx** <term>Kalck</term> <note>a powdery metallic oxide produced by heating or chemical action</note> using **spirit or water of Vitriol** <note>original Latin: *Spiritu vel Aqua Vitrioli*; sulfuric acid</note>, **spirit of salt** <note>original Latin: *Spiritu Salis*; hydrochloric acid</note>, and copper plates. This also happens to mercury if one draws a **spirit of nitre** <note>original Latin: *Spiritum Nitri*; nitric acid</note> or good **strong water** over it several times in a flask or a **retort** <term>Retorten</term>, whereby a **precipitated mercury** <note>original Latin: *Mercurius praecipitatus*</note> is obtained as a powder.

**To Pulverize** <term>Pulverisiren</term> is: When one pounds, rubs, and sieves a hard material in a mortar, on a grinding stone, and through a sieve into a fine powder.

**To Putrefy** <term>Putreficiren</term> is: When one places a moist, watery, spirituous, or oily substance in a glass or other vessel in gentle heat for a time, and allows it to break down and rot therein; from which the dissolved spirit is subsequently obtained much more easily.

**To Rectify** <term>Rectificiren</term> has this meaning: That when one has a prepared spirit or an oil which is not perfectly pure, and has not been separated from its impurities, it must be driven over the **helm** <note>the "alembic" or cap of the distillation apparatus</note> one, two, or even more times.

**To Reduce** <term>Reduciren</term> is: When a metal has been destroyed—such as by **Royal Water** and **Strong Water** and other corrosive **solvents** <term>Menstrua</term>—so that it looks like a **calx** or cannot be recognized as metal at all, it must be melted back into a **body** <term>Corpus</term> <note>a solid, metallic state</note> with a good **flux powder** <term>Fluß-Pulver</term>. This must be done with borax, saltpeter, potash, salts, and the like, all of which have been well **dulcified** <note>original German: *ausgesüsset*; the process of washing away corrosive salts with water</note> beforehand.

**To Precipitate** <term>Praecipitiren</term> means: When gold dissolved in **Royal Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua Regis*; a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids</note> or silver dissolved in **Strong Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua forti*; nitric acid</note> is caused to fall and be cast down into a **calx** <term>Kalck</term> <note>a powdery metallic oxide produced by heating or chemical action</note> using **Spirit or Oil of Vitriol** <note>original: *Spiritu vel Aqua Vitrioli*; sulfuric acid</note>, **Spirit of Salt** <note>original: *Spiritu Salis*; hydrochloric acid</note>, and copper sheets. **To Rectify** <term>Rectificiren</term> is understood as: When one has a prepared spirit or an oil that is not perfectly pure and has not been separated from its excess <note>referring to surplus water or phlegm</note>, it must be passed one or more times, and even more often, over the **alembic head** <term>Helm</term> <note>the cap of a still used to collect and direct vapors</note>.

**To Reiterate** <term>Reiteriren</term> is: When one repeats a task, whatever it may be, and begins the work over again from the start.

**To Resolve** <term>Resolviren</term> is: When one leads a metal or mineral back into its first essence, or transforms such a thing into **living mercury** <note>original Latin: *Mercurium viuum*; liquid quicksilver, often considered the "root" of all metals in alchemical theory</note>.

**To Reverberate** <term>Reverberiren</term> is: When one thoroughly heats a previously prepared **calx** <term>Kalck</term> <note>a powdery metallic oxide</note> or powder—whether of gold, silver, or another material—on a **cupel** <term>Schörben</term> under a **muffle** <note>a ceramic enclosure that protects the substance from the fuel but allows heat and flame to "reverberate" or reflect onto it</note> or on a small broad dish in a furnace adapted for this purpose, wherein the flame can strike over the material to drive off any volatile parts still clinging to it; during this process, the material must be constantly stirred with a small iron rake.

**To Separate** <term>Separiren</term> is: When one divides the spirit from the oil using a funnel, or the **spirit** <term>Spiritum</term> from the **phlegm** <term>Phlegmate</term> <note>original: *Phlegmate*; the watery, tasteless, and inactive part of a distilled substance</note> or wateriness by means of a flask through **distillation** <note>original Latin: *per Distillationem*</note>, thereby parting the pure from the impure.

**To Seal** <term>Sigilliren</term> is: When one closes a flask, a vial, or a **retort** <term>Retort</term> with an attached **receiver** <term>Recipienten</term> **hermetically** <note>original Latin: *hermetice*; an airtight seal, traditionally made by melting the glass neck of a vessel</note>, sealing it with heat, or plugging and coating it with lutes made of dough, lime, and other adhesives, or encasing it in clay, so that no spirit—and thus the finest spiritual power—can escape.

**To Dissolve** <term>Solviren</term> is: When one dissolves gold, silver, or other metals and minerals, as well as salts and grown crystals, in **Royal Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua Regis*; a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold</note>, **Strong Water** <note>original Latin: *Aqua forti*; nitric acid</note>, or in a strong spirit and suitable water; for which glass separation-flasks are required.

**To Stratify** <term>Stratificiren</term> **is:** When one covers thin-beaten or cut metal sheets, or finely granulated metal, with other minerals, salts, or cementing powders in a crucible or a box and **lutes** it <note>seals it with airtight clay or "lute"</note>, in order to **cement** it <note>a dry-heating process to refine or alter the metal's properties</note> and transfer the power, increase, or improvement from one material into the other. For this, one must place a layer of the cementing powder at the bottom of the box or crucible, then a layer of the metal sheets, and so on, adding one layer after another to form a sequence of **layer upon layer** <note>original Latin: *Stratum super Stratum*</note>: this is what is called "stratifying."

**To Sublime** <term>Sublimiren</term> **is:** When one drives **living mercury** <note>original Latin: *Mercurium viuum*; liquid quicksilver</note>, sulfur, or antimony and **sal ammoniac** <term>Salmiac</term> <note>ammonium chloride, used as a flux</note> upwards with appropriate fire in a flask or other sublimating vessel placed in a sand-bath <note>original: *Sand-Capelle*; a container filled with sand to provide even, indirect heat</note>, closed with either a "blind" <note>a cap without a spout</note> or an open **helm** <note>the top part of a still, also called an alembic</note>.

**To Tinge** <term>Tingiren</term> **is:** When one introduces a prepared philosophical tincture or powder into an imperfect metal that is in a state of flux <note>molten or melted</note>, uniting it with the metal through melting and thereby **transmuting** <note>transforming one substance into another</note> it into gold or silver.

**To Volatilize** <term>Volatilisiren</term> **means, lastly:** When one makes a fixed salt volatile through frequent **cohobations** <term>Cohobia</term> <note>the process of pouring a distilled liquid back onto the solid residue and re-distilling it multiple times</note> with a spirit, and finally leads it upward, even over the helm of the vessel.

### Appendix.

Inasmuch as the foundation for reaching the **Universal Tincture** <term>Vniuersal-Tinctur</term> <note>the "Philosopher's Stone" or "Great Elixir" capable of curing all diseases and perfecting metals</note> via the **wet way** <note>original Latin: *Via humida*; a liquid-based alchemical path using acids and solutions</note> has been sufficiently shown to the seeker in the preceding pages; now, the seeker shall also be duly informed, as desired, regarding the **dry philosophical way** <note>a high-heat method using crucibles and furnaces rather than liquid solvents</note> practiced by the ancient father **Morienus** <note>Morienus Romanus, a legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist</note> and **Geber** <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan, an 8th-century polymath and "father of chemistry"</note>—both kings and masters of this great secret—as well as other **Adepts** <note>original Latin: *Adeptorum*; those who have successfully discovered the Great Work</note>.

To do this, a layer of the <term>cementing powder</term> must be placed at the bottom of the box or crucible, followed by a layer of the metal sheets, and so forth, adding one layer after another, thus forming **layer upon layer** <note>original Latin: *Stratum super Stratum*</note>: which is called stratifying.

**To Sublimate** <term>Sublimiren</term> **is:** When one drives upward with appropriate fire a **living mercury** <note>original Latin: *Mercurium viuum*; liquid quicksilver</note>, a sulfur, or an antimony and sal ammoniac in a flask or other subliming vessel within a **sand bath** <note>original: *Sand-Capelle*; a container of sand used to provide even, indirect heat</note>, sealed with a blind or open **alembic head** <note>original: *Helme*; the cap of a distilling vessel that collects vapors</note>.

**To Tinge** <term>Tingiren</term> **is:** When one adds a prepared philosophical tincture or powder into an imperfect metal held in flux <note>melted into a liquid state</note>, uniting it with the metal through melting and transmuting it into gold or silver.

**Lastly, to Volatilize** <term>Volatilisiren</term> **means:** When one makes a fixed salt volatile through frequent **re-distillations** <note>original: <term>Cohobia</term>; the process of repeatedly pouring a distilled liquid back onto its solid residue and re-distilling to concentrate its power</note> with a spirit, and finally drives it upward, even over the alembic head.

## Axiom of the Adepts:
<note>original Latin: *Axioma Adeptorum*</note>

Our work is made from two Mercurial Substances: from the Pure (that is: from **Gold** <note>original Latin: *Auro*</note>), the Crude purified (that is: from the **Martial Regulus of Antimony** <note>original Latin: *Regulo Antimonii Martiali*; a metallic form of antimony refined using iron, associated with Mars</note>), and joined by the Fire of Friendship (that is: from **Animated Mercury** <note>original Latin: *Mercurio Animato*; mercury that has been "quickened" or prepared for the Work</note>).

### Another Axiom.

Our work consists of these three: of **Gold**, **the Moon** <note>Luna/Silver</note>, and **Mercury**. By Gold or the Sun, we understand **pure gold**. By the Moon, we understand **our Silver**, or the Martial Regulus of Antimony. Therefore, he who knows how to **tinge** <note>transform or dye</note> Mercury with the Sun and Moon has arrived at the Art.

### Another Axiom.

Our **living silver** <note>original Latin: *Argentum viuum*; quicksilver</note> is a most clear Water (that is: Mercury prepared through seven or nine **Eagles** <note>alchemical term for cycles of sublimation or distillation</note>); our **Arsenic** is pure Silver (that is: Martial Regulus of Antimony); and our **Sulfur** is pure Gold. In these three, all Perfection consists. So says **Arnold of Villanova** <note>a famous 13th-century physician and alchemist</note>.

...the perfect bodies, which have been joined with our Regulus <term>The "regulus" refers to the metallic heart or purified mass of a substance, often associated with antimony in this period of alchemy.</term>, are completely dissolved and reduced into an incredibly oily powder.

### Chapter VII.

Our Silver <note>original: *Argentum*</note> is pure Silver; that is: our Moon <note>original: *Luna*</note> and our purified Regulus <note>original: *Regulus purificatus*</note>. However, the reason it is called Arsenic <note>original: *Arsenicum*</note> is because it changes both gold and other red bodies joined with it into its own snow-white color. Just as arsenic instantly turns red copper into its white color during the melting process, so too does our Regulus instantly change all perfect and imperfect bodies into its shining white color. This is called by us the "reddening of the bodies" <note>While the text says "white color," the alchemist clarifies that this transformation is part of the process of preparing red metallic bodies for the next stage.</note>, or the transformation of the perfect metallic bodies into the first matter <note>original: *Materia prima*</note>, that is, into our Mercury <note>original: *Mercurium nostrum*</note>.

Regarding this, our Sendivogius <note>Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636) was a famous Polish alchemist known for his theories on the "food of life" in the air.</note> reports: After Saturn <note>In alchemy, Saturn usually represents lead or the "heavy," dark stage of the process.</note> had drawn ten parts of our water, he took one part of the fruit from the Sun-Tree <note>A poetic reference to gold.</note> and placed it inside; and the fruit of the Sun-Tree melted in such water like ice in warm water. Thus, this highly shining Regulus of ours was named by Saturn with its rightful name: the Water of Life <note>original: *Aqua vitae*</note>. For this water, says Saturn, is devoted to the Sun-Fruit like a wife to a husband; that is: the Sun-Fruit is the gold, the man, or the active agent <note>original: *agens*</note>; our Regulus or Dry Water <note>original: *Aqua sicca*</note> is the Water of Life, or the passive recipient <note>original: *patiens*</note>. For the male, solar seed can be purified, unlocked, and putrefied <note>the process of breaking down a substance through heat and moisture</note> in no other water than this highly shining Water of Life, and specifically by means of our secret fire.

<summary>This page explains that the alchemical "Regulus" acts as a solvent that turns gold and other metals into a white "first matter" or "Water of Life." It uses the metaphor of a marriage between the male gold (Sun-fruit) and the female solvent to describe the purification of the metallic seed.</summary>
